articles.body: The change to make now Clerk’s machine-to-machine (M2M) tokens reached general availability on October 14, 2026. If your application has background workers or backend services calling one another, this is a good moment to review which credentials they use and what the new usage model could cost. It is not a reason to replace user sessions or every existing API key. Clerk describes M2M tokens as credentials for communication between machines in your own infrastructure. Its GA announcement says the APIs are stable for production, and adds dashboard charts for token creation and verification activity. The announcement also reiterates planned usage charges, but says billing is not live and that Clerk will provide at least 30 days’ notice before it begins.

articles.body: AutoLensAI composites photographs of real vehicles into virtual studios for dealership listings. The setting changes. The vehicle's bodywork, equipment, cabin, and visible condition have to survive that change. The windows make this harder than the outline suggests. A side window can show a headrest, a reflection of a building behind the photographer, and another car visible through the far side of the cabin. Move the vehicle into a studio and pieces of the parking lot can come with it. Remove too much and the headrest goes too. In Negative Space Is a Label , I wrote about teaching a matting model to reject shadows and floor reflections beside a vehicle. A dark patch touching a tire can still be background.

articles.title: The Latency Budget: Designing Response Timing Before You Automate a Single Reply
articles.excerpt: Teams evaluating support automation usually start with the question "what should the bot say?" The more revealing question is "when should each party speak?" Response timing is invisible when it works…
articles.body: Teams evaluating support automation usually start with the question "what should the bot say?" The more revealing question is "when should each party speak?" Response timing is invisible when it works and relationship-destroying when it does not: an instant reply at 3 a.m. reads as helpful; an instant reply ten seconds after a frustrated paragraph reads as a wall. Before wiring any auto-responder, design a latency budget. Three clocks run at once Every support conversation has three timing expectations stacked on top of each other. The buyer expects a first acknowledgment quickly — minutes, not hours, during business hours. The marketplace (if you sell on one) expects a response-time score to stay above its threshold, and it measures every inbound message whether you answer well or badly.

articles.title: i stopped trusting coding agent demos, so i built a tool that interviews them
articles.excerpt: i kept trusting agent demos more than i should have, so i built a small runner that makes coding agents prove it on my own tasks. the idea is boring on purpose: point it at any repo, define a few task…
articles.body: i kept trusting agent demos more than i should have, so i built a small runner that makes coding agents prove it on my own tasks. the idea is boring on purpose: point it at any repo, define a few tasks in plain json, and it runs each agent CLI on a throwaway copy of the project. after the agent finishes, the verify scripts get restored from the source repo before they run. that part matters. an agent with write access can just edit its own checker and pass. i shipped agent-trials without the restore step, audited it, felt dumb, fixed it. a real run on a 3-task toy suite looked like this: opus sonnet haiku fix-clamp 33.2s 39.5s 32.6s divide-guard 22.8s 26.8s 90.5s slug-test 42.7s 67.5s 45.5s score 3/3 3/3 3/3 scores and medians move around between runs.

articles.title: GGUF vs safetensors — the runtime decides, not the format
articles.excerpt: Originally published on mrsaynothing.dev · 14 October 2026. The record read, not run — every number below is checkable with one curl. DuckDuckGo autocompletes gguf vs safetensors as if it were a cage…
articles.body: Originally published on mrsaynothing.dev · 14 October 2026. The record read, not run — every number below is checkable with one curl . DuckDuckGo autocompletes gguf vs safetensors as if it were a cage fight between two file extensions. It is a gate check. Pick GGUF and one shelf of runtimes opens — llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, Jan. Pick safetensors and a different shelf opens — transformers, vLLM, ComfyUI. The format is the list of doors that will open; everything else follows. The lie this piece refuses: that the fight is decided by speed numbers nobody has matched on the same box. What the record gives you for free — and what most arguments skip — is what each container weighs, and where each one can even be opened. What are you actually choosing between?
articles.author: Mr Say Nothing

articles.title: A Passing Test Can Still Prove Nothing
articles.excerpt: Some of the most misleading tests are not flaky, slow, or obviously incomplete. They are fast, deterministic, and green. They also pass for the wrong reason. That is especially dangerous in fault-tole…
articles.body: Some of the most misleading tests are not flaky, slow, or obviously incomplete. They are fast, deterministic, and green. They also pass for the wrong reason. That is especially dangerous in fault-tolerant code. A test may claim that a failed dependency is contained, a fallback runs, or an established workflow continues. Yet its assertion may observe an outcome that can occur both before and after the recovery boundary. The suite reports confidence while the behaviour named by the test remains unproved. The false-positive shape Imagine a dispatcher with an optional policy source in front of an established workflow. The intended behaviour is straightforward: Ask the policy source whether the old workflow should stand down. If that optional source fails, contain the fault.

articles.body: Imagine starting your workday to find that an AI system has already organized customer requests, reviewed incoming reports, identified potential problems, and prepared several tasks for your approval. Instead of spending hours moving information between applications, you begin by reviewing the work an AI agent has completed. This is the promise behind agentic AI, one of the most significant developments in enterprise artificial intelligence. AI has already changed how we write, research, analyze information, and solve problems. But in 2026, the conversation is increasingly moving beyond generating answers toward systems that can plan tasks, use digital tools, and execute multiple steps toward a defined goal. I believe this creates an important opportunity for businesses.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the " Whirlpool Galaxy , " also known as Messier 51, or M51. Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy. Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies. Spiral galaxy M51 (NGC 5194), The Whirlpool Galaxy, displays its long arms which consist of stars and gas laced with dust arranged in long lanes, in this view from the Hubble Space Telescope.

articles.title: 'We basically did Top Gun in space': 'Star Trek Starfleet Academy' warps back into action in March 2027 for sophomore year in the final frontier
articles.excerpt: The sophomore season of "Star Trek: Starfleet Academy" will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+.
articles.body: NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date. The sophomore season of " Star Trek: Starfleet Academy " will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+ . The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10). "Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel.

articles.title: See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York
articles.excerpt: This iconic spaceship will now live long and prosper in its brand-new Star Trek Tour home.
articles.body: Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft. After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.
